translations.literal: Jing Province
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史，漢治武陵漢壽，魏、晉治江陵，王敦治武昌，陶侃前治沔陽，後治武昌，王廙治江陵，庾亮治武昌，庾翼進襄陽，復還夏口，桓溫治江陵，桓沖治上明，王忱還江陵，此後遂治江陵。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province: under the Han the seat was at Hanshou in Wuling; under Wei and Jin it was at Jiangling. Wang Dun governed from Wuchang; Tao Kan first from Mianyang, later from Wuchang; Wang Yi from Jiangling; Yu Liang from Wuchang; Yu Yi advanced to Xiangyang and then returned to Xiakou; Huan Wen from Jiangling; Huan Chong from Shangming; Wang Chen returned to Jiangling—after which the seat remained at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector of Jing: in Han times the seat lay at Hanshou in Wuling; under Wei and Jin at Jiangling. Wang Dun held court at Wuchang; Tao Kan first at Mianyang, then at Wuchang; Wang Yi at Jiangling; Yu Liang at Wuchang; Yu Yi advanced to Xiangyang and fell back to Xiakou; Huan Wen at Jiangling; Huan Chong at Shangming; Wang Chen back at Jiangling—from then on the provincial seat stayed at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 宋初領郡三十一，後分南陽、順陽、襄陽、新野、竟陵為雍州，湘川十郡為湘州，江夏、武陵屬郢州，隨郡、義陽屬司州，北義陽省，凡餘十一郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song it oversaw thirty-one commanderies; later Nanyang, Shunyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Jingling were split off as Yong Province, the ten commanderies of the Xiang region as Xiang Province, Jiangxia and Wuling assigned to Ying Province, Sui Commandery and Yiyang to Si Province, Northern Yiyang abolished—eleven commanderies remained in all.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liu Song it governed thirty-one commanderies; later Nanyang, Shunyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Jingling were carved out as Yong, ten Xiang River commanderies as Xiang, Jiangxia and Wuling went to Ying, Sui and Yiyang to Si, Northern Yiyang was abolished, and eleven commanderies were left.

sentences.zh: 文帝世，又立宋安左郡，領拓邊、綏慕、樂寧、慕化、仰澤、革音、歸德七縣，後省改。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wen's reign Song'an Left Commandery was also established, overseeing the seven counties of Tuobian, Suimu, Lening, Muhua, Yangze, Geyin, and Guide; it was later abolished and reorganized.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen, Song'an Left Commandery was added with seven counties—Tuobian, Suimu, Lening, Muhua, Yangze, Geyin, and Guide—then later abolished and reorganized.

translations.literal: Wenyang Commandery was also transferred to belong here.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyang Commandery was transferred here as well.

translations.literal: It now oversees twelve commanderies and forty-eight counties.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs twelve commanderies and forty-eight counties.

translations.literal: Households: 65,604.
translations.idiomatic: Registered households: 65,604.

sentences.zh: 去京都水三千三百八十。

translations.literal: Distance to the capital by water route: 3,380.
translations.idiomatic: 3,380 li from the capital by water.

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Nan Commandery, established under Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Nan Commandery: established under the Qin.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝元年，為臨江國，景帝中二年復故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gaozu of Han it became the State of Linjiang; in the second year of the middle Jingdi era it reverted to the former status.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozu's first year it became the kingdom of Linjiang; in Jingdi's middle era, year 2, it reverted.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年改曰新郡，尋復故。

translations.literal: In Taikang year 1 of Emperor Wu of Jin it was renamed Xinjun Commandery, but soon reverted to the former name.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang year 1 of Jin Emperor Wu it was briefly renamed Xinjun, then restored.

sentences.zh: 宋初領縣九，後州陵、監利度屬巴陵；

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song it oversaw nine counties; later Zhouling and Jianli were transferred to belong to Baling;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song it had nine counties; later Zhouling and Jianli were reassigned to Baling;

sentences.zh: 旌陽文帝元嘉十八年省併枝江。

translations.literal: Jingyang was abolished and merged into Zhijiang in the eighteenth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 18 of Emperor Wen, Jingyang was abolished and merged into Zhijiang.

sentences.zh: 二漢無旌陽，見晉太康地志，疑是吳所立。

translations.literal: Neither Former nor Later Han had Jingyang; it appears in the Jin Taikang Territorial Treatise—presumably established by Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyang does not appear in either Han; the Jin Taikang treatise lists it, so it was probably a Wu foundation.

translations.literal: Six counties remained in all.
translations.idiomatic: Six counties remained.

translations.literal: Households: 14,544; persons: 75,087.
translations.idiomatic: 14,544 households and 75,087 persons.

translations.literal: Jiangling: Chancellor of the Dukedom; a Han-era old county.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling (Chancellor of the Dukedom): a county dating to the Han.

sentences.zh: :華容公相，漢舊縣，晉武太康元年省，後復立。

translations.literal: Huarong: Chancellor of the Dukedom; a Han-era old county, abolished in Taikang year 1 of Jin Emperor Wu, later re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Huarong (Chancellor of the Dukedom): an old Han county, abolished in Jin Taikang year 1 and later restored.

translations.literal: Dangyang: Chancellor of the Barony; a Han-era old county.
translations.idiomatic: Dangyang (Chancellor of the Barony): a Han-era county.

translations.literal: Linju: Chancellor of the Earldom; a Han-era old county.
translations.idiomatic: Linju (Chancellor of the Earldom): a Han-era county.

sentences.zh: 晉太康、永寧地志屬襄陽，後度。

translations.literal: The Jin Taikang and Yongning territorial treatises place it under Xiangyang; it was later transferred.
translations.idiomatic: The Taikang and Yongning treatises assign it to Xiangyang; it was later reassigned.

translations.literal: Bian County: Chancellor of the Barony; a Han-era old county.
translations.idiomatic: Bian (Chancellor of the Barony): a Han-era county.

translations.literal: Zhijiang: Chancellor of the Marquisate; a Han-era old county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijiang (Chancellor of the Marquisate): a Han-era county.

sentences.zh: 南平內史，吳南郡治江南，領江陵、華容諸縣。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Nanping: under Wu, Nan Commandery administered the south of the Yangzi and oversaw Jiangling, Huarong, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Minister of Nanping: in Wu times Nan Commandery governed the south bank and held Jiangling, Huarong, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康元年，分南郡江南為南平郡，治作唐，後治江安。

translations.literal: In Taikang year 1 of Jin Emperor Wu, the south of the Yangzi in Nan Commandery was split off as Nanping Commandery, with its seat at Zuotang, later at Jiang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Taikang year 1 of Jin Emperor Wu the Jiangnan portion of Nan was carved out as Nanping, first seated at Zuotang, later at Jiang'an.

translations.literal: It oversaw four counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed four counties.

sentences.zh: 戶一萬二千三百九十二，口四萬五千四十九。

translations.literal: Households: 12,392; persons: 45,049.
translations.idiomatic: 12,392 households and 45,049 persons.

translations.literal: Distance to the provincial seat by water: 250.
translations.idiomatic: 250 li from the provincial seat by water.

sentences.zh: 去京都水三千五百，無陸。

translations.literal: Distance to the capital by water: 3,500; no land route.
translations.idiomatic: 3,500 li from the capital by water; no overland route.

sentences.zh: :江安侯相，晉武帝太康元年立。

translations.literal: Jiang'an: Chancellor of the Marquisate; established in Taikang year 1 of Jin Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang'an (Chancellor of the Marquisate): founded in Jin Taikang year 1.

sentences.zh: :孱陵侯相，二漢舊縣，屬武陵，晉太康地志屬南平。

translations.literal: Chanling: Chancellor of the Marquisate; an old county of both Han dynasties, belonging to Wuling; the Jin Taikang treatise places it under Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Chanling (Chancellor of the Marquisate): a county of both Han, once in Wuling; the Jin Taikang treatise lists it under Nanping.

sentences.zh: :作唐侯相，前漢無，後漢屬武陵，晉太康地志屬南平。

translations.literal: Zuotang: Chancellor of the Marquisate; absent in Former Han, under Wuling in Later Han; the Jin Taikang treatise places it under Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Zuotang (Chancellor of the Marquisate): not in Former Han, in Wuling under Later Han; the Jin Taikang treatise assigns it to Nanping.

translations.literal: Nan'an: Magistrate; split off from Jiang'an by Jin Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an (Magistrate): carved out of Jiang'an under Jin Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 天門太守，吳孫休永安六年，分武陵立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Tianmen: in the sixth year of Yong'an under Sun Xiu of Wu, split off from Wuling and established.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Tianmen: created in Yong'an year 6 of Wu's Sun Xiu by splitting Wuling.

sentences.zh: 充縣有松梁山，山有石，石開處數十丈，其高以努仰射不至，其上名「天門」，因此名郡。

translations.literal: Chong County has Mount Songliang; on the mountain is a rock with an opening tens of zhang wide, so high that an arrow shot upward from a crossbow cannot reach the top; the summit is called "Heaven's Gate," whence the commandery takes its name.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had Mount Songliang, where a rock gaped tens of zhang across—too high for an upward crossbow shot to reach—and the peak was called Heaven's Gate, giving the commandery its name.

translations.literal: Chong County was later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Chong County was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建元年，度郢州，明帝泰始三年復舊。

translations.literal: In Xiaojian year 1 of Emperor Xiaowu it was transferred to Ying Province; in Taishi year 3 of Emperor Ming it reverted to the former arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian year 1 of Emperor Xiaowu it went to Ying; in Taishi year 3 of Emperor Ming it was restored.

translations.literal: It oversaw four counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed four counties.

translations.literal: Households: 3,195.
translations.idiomatic: 3,195 households.

translations.idiomatic: 1,200 li from the provincial seat by water, 600 by land.

translations.literal: Distance to the capital by water: 3,500.
translations.idiomatic: 3,500 li from the capital by water.

translations.idiomatic: Liyang (Magistrate): founded in Jin Taikang year 4.

translations.literal: Linli: Magistrate; established in Taikang year 4 of Jin Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Linli (Magistrate): founded in Jin Taikang year 4.

translations.literal: Lingyang: Magistrate; a Han-era old county belonging to Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyang (Magistrate): a Han-era county in Wuling.

sentences.zh: :漊中令，二漢無，晉太康地志有，疑是吳立。

translations.literal: Louzhong: Magistrate; absent in both Han dynasties but listed in the Jin Taikang treatise—presumably established by Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Louzhong (Magistrate): not in either Han but in the Jin Taikang treatise, probably a Wu foundation.

sentences.zh: 宜都太守，太康地志、王隱地道、何志並云吳分南郡立；

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Yidu: the Taikang Territorial Treatise, Wang Yin's Treatise on the Land, and He's Treatise all say Wu split it off from Nan Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Yidu: the Taikang treatise, Wang Yin's land treatise, and He's treatise all say Wu carved it from Nan Commandery;

translations.literal: Zhang Bo's Records of Wu says Liu Bei established it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bo's Records of Wu credits Liu Bei with founding it.

sentences.zh: 按吳志，呂蒙平南郡，據江陵，陸遜別取宜都，獲秭歸、枝江、夷道縣。

translations.literal: According to the History of Wu, Lü Meng pacified Nan Commandery and held Jiangling; Lu Xun separately took Yidu and captured the counties of Zigui, Zhijiang, and Yidao.
translations.idiomatic: The History of Wu records that Lü Meng pacified Nan and seized Jiangling, while Lu Xun took Yidu and captured Zigui, Zhijiang, and Yidao.

sentences.zh: 初權與劉備分荊州，而南郡屬備，則是備分南郡立宜都，非吳立也。

translations.literal: At first Sun Quan and Liu Bei divided Jing Province, and Nan Commandery belonged to Bei—thus Bei split Nan Commandery to establish Yidu, not Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan and Liu Bei first divided Jing, Nan belonged to Bei, so Bei—not Wu—split Nan to create Yidu.

sentences.zh: 習鑿齒云，魏武平荊州，分南郡枝江以西為臨江郡，建安十五年，劉備改為宜都。

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi says that when Emperor Wu of Wei pacified Jing Province, the region west of Zhijiang in Nan Commandery was made Linjiang Commandery; in the fifteenth year of Jian'an, Liu Bei renamed it Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zuochi writes that after Cao Cao pacified Jing, everything west of Zhijiang in Nan became Linjiang; in Jian'an year 15 Liu Bei renamed it Yidu.

translations.literal: It oversaw four counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed four counties.

sentences.zh: 戶一千八百四十三，口三萬四千二百二十。

translations.literal: Households: 1,843; persons: 34,220.
translations.idiomatic: 1,843 households and 34,220 persons.

translations.literal: Distance to the provincial seat by water: 350; no land route.
translations.idiomatic: 350 li from the provincial seat by water; no overland route.

translations.literal: Distance to the capital by water: 3,730.
translations.idiomatic: 3,730 li from the capital by water.

translations.literal: Yidao: Magistrate; a Han-era old county.
translations.idiomatic: Yidao (Magistrate): a Han-era county.

sentences.zh: :佷山男相，前漢屬武陵，後漢屬南郡，晉武帝太康元年改為興山，後復舊。

translations.literal: Henshan: Chancellor of the Barony; under Former Han it belonged to Wuling, under Later Han to Nan Commandery; in Taikang year 1 of Jin Emperor Wu it was renamed Xingshan, later restored to the former name.
translations.idiomatic: Henshan (Chancellor of the Barony): in Former Han part of Wuling, in Later Han of Nan; Jin Taikang year 1 renamed it Xingshan, then the old name returned.

translations.literal: Yichang: Magistrate; He's Treatise says established by Jin Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yichang (Magistrate): He's treatise dates it to Jin Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 按太康、永寧地志並無，疑是此後所立。

translations.literal: According to the Taikang and Yongning treatises it is absent—presumably established afterward.
translations.idiomatic: It does not appear in the Taikang or Yongning treatises, so it was probably founded later.

sentences.zh: :夷陵令，漢舊縣，吳改曰西陵，晉武帝太康元年復舊。

translations.literal: Yiling: Magistrate; a Han-era old county; Wu renamed it Xiling; in Taikang year 1 of Jin Emperor Wu the former name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yiling (Magistrate): a Han county renamed Xiling under Wu, restored in Jin Taikang year 1.

sentences.zh: 巴東公相，譙周巴記云，初平元年，荊州帳下司馬趙韙建議分巴郡諸縣安漢以下為永寧郡。

translations.literal: Chancellor of the Dukedom of Badong: Qiao Zhou's Record of Ba says that in the first year of Chuping, Staff Major Zhao Wei of Jing Province proposed splitting off the Ba commandery counties from Anhan southward as Yongning Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of the Dukedom of Badong: Qiao Zhou's Record of Ba records that in Chuping year 1 Zhao Wei, staff major of Jing, proposed carving the Ba counties from Anhan downward into Yongning Commandery.

sentences.zh: 建安六年，劉璋改永寧為巴東郡，以涪陵縣分立丹興、漢葭二縣，立巴東屬國都尉，後為涪陵郡。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jian'an, Liu Zhang changed Yongning to Badong Commandery, split Fuling County to establish Danxing and Hanjia counties, set up the Commandant of the Badong Dependent State, later [renamed as] Fuling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an year 6 Liu Zhang renamed Yongning Badong, split Fuling to create Danxing and Hanjia, and installed a commandant of the Badong dependent state—later Fuling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉太康地志，巴東屬梁州，惠帝太安二年度益州，穆帝永和初平蜀，度屬荊州。

translations.literal: The Jin Taikang treatise places Badong under Liang Province; in Taian year 2 of Emperor Hui it was transferred to Yi Province; when Emperor Mu pacified Shu at the beginning of Yonghe, it was transferred to belong to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Taikang treatise lists Badong under Liang; in Taian year 2 of Emperor Hui it went to Yi; after Emperor Mu pacified Shu at the start of Yonghe it was reassigned to Jing.

sentences.zh: 永初郡國志無巴渠、黽陽二縣。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commandery and State Gazetteer lacks the two counties of Baqu and Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu gazetteer does not list Baqu or Mengyang.

translations.literal: It oversaw seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed seven counties.

sentences.zh: 戶一萬三千七百九十五，口四萬五千二百三十七。

translations.literal: Households: 13,795; persons: 45,237.
translations.idiomatic: 13,795 households and 45,237 persons.

translations.idiomatic: 1,300 li from the provincial seat by water.

translations.idiomatic: 4,680 li from the capital by water.

sentences.zh: :魚復侯相，漢舊縣，屬巴郡，劉備章武二年，改為永安，晉武帝太康元年復舊。

translations.literal: Yufu: Chancellor of the Marquisate; a Han-era old county belonging to Ba Commandery; in the second year of Zhangwu under Liu Bei it was renamed Yong'an; in Taikang year 1 of Jin Emperor Wu the former name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Yufu (Chancellor of the Marquisate): a Han county in Ba, renamed Yong'an in Liu Bei's Zhangwu year 2, restored in Jin Taikang year 1.

translations.literal: Xuyu: Magistrate; a Han-era old county belonging to Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyu (Magistrate): a Han-era county in Ba.

translations.literal: Xinpu: Magistrate; newly established according to He's Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Xinpu (Magistrate): a new foundation per He's treatise.

sentences.zh: :南浦令，劉禪建興八年十月，益州牧閻宇表改羊渠立。

translations.literal: Nanpu: Magistrate; in the tenth month of the eighth year of Jianxing under Liu Shan, Governor of Yi Province Yan Yu memorialized to change Yangqu and establish it.
translations.idiomatic: Nanpu (Magistrate): in the tenth month of Jianxing year 8 Liu Shan's Yi governor Yan Yu petitioned to rename Yangqu and establish this county.

translations.literal: Yangqu is not further described; He's Treatise says Wu established it.
translations.idiomatic: Yangqu is otherwise unknown; He's treatise says Wu founded it.

translations.literal: Hanfeng: Magistrate; He's Treatise does not note when it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Hanfeng (Magistrate): He's treatise gives no date of establishment.

sentences.zh: 太康地志巴東有漢昌縣，疑是。

translations.literal: The Taikang treatise lists Hanchang County in Badong—presumably the same place.
translations.idiomatic: The Taikang treatise lists Hanchang in Badong, which is probably the same county.

translations.literal: Baqu: Magistrate; He's Treatise does not note when it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Baqu (Magistrate): He's treatise gives no date of establishment.

translations.literal: Mengyang: Magistrate; He's Treatise does not note when it was established.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang (Magistrate): He's treatise gives no date of establishment.

sentences.zh: 晉末平吳時，峽中立武陵郡，有黽陽、黔陽縣，咸寧元年並省。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified at the end of Jin, Wuling Commandery was established in the gorges with the counties of Mengyang and Qianyang; in the first year of Xianning both were abolished together.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jin conquest of Wu a Wuling commandery was set up in the gorges with Mengyang and Qianyang; both were abolished in Xianning year 1.

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Wenyang: newly established according to He's Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Wenyang: a new foundation per He's treatise.

sentences.zh: 先屬梁州，文帝元嘉十一年度。

translations.literal: It first belonged to Liang Province; in the eleventh year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen it was transferred.
translations.idiomatic: It was first under Liang; in Yuanjia year 11 of Emperor Wen it was reassigned.

sentences.zh: 宋初有四縣，後省汶陽縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song it had four counties; later Wenyang County was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song it had four counties; Wenyang County was later abolished.

translations.literal: It now oversees three counties.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs three counties.

sentences.zh: 戶九百五十八，口四千九百一十四。

translations.literal: Households: 958; persons: 4,914.
translations.idiomatic: 958 households and 4,914 persons.

translations.idiomatic: 700 li from the provincial seat by water, 400 by land.

translations.idiomatic: 4,100 li from the capital.

translations.idiomatic: Tongyang (Magistrate): a new foundation per He's treatise.

translations.idiomatic: Juyang (Magistrate): a new foundation per He's treatise.

translations.idiomatic: Gao'an (Magistrate): a new foundation per He's treatise.

translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Yiyang,

translations.literal: 〈Yiyang Commandery is treated separately.〉
translations.idiomatic: (Yiyang Commandery is discussed elsewhere.)

translations.literal: At the end of Jin it was established as a frontier administration for displaced persons from Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jin it was set up as a refugee commandery for people displaced from Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 宋初有四縣，孝武孝建二年，以平陽縣併厥西。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song it had four counties; in the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, Pingyang County was merged into Juexi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song it had four counties; in Xiaojian year 2 of Emperor Xiaowu Pingyang was merged into Juexi.

translations.literal: Pingyang had originally been a commandery; south of the Yangzi it was established as a frontier administration.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang had once been a full commandery, re-established south of the Yangzi as a refugee district.

sentences.zh: 魏世分河東為平陽郡，晉末省為縣。

translations.literal: In Wei times Hedong was split to form Pingyang Commandery; at the end of Jin it was reduced to a county.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, Pingyang was carved from Hedong; by the end of Jin it had been reduced to a county.

translations.literal: It now oversees two counties.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs two counties.

sentences.zh: 戶一千六百七，口九千七百四十一。
